research_question: What is the effect of a single sympathetic nerve block, compared with standard care, on pain score at 14 days post-intervention?
treatment_label: Single sympathetic nerve block (e.g. stellate ganglion, lumbar sympathetic, celiac plexus, or paravertebral sympathetic block)
control_label: Standard care (usual pharmacological/conservative management, sham block, or placebo injection)
outcome_description: Patient-reported pain intensity score measured at approximately 14 days (±a few days) after the single sympathetic nerve block, on any continuous pain scale (e.g. VAS 0-100, NRS 0-10, pain subscale of a composite instrument). Only the ~14-day assessment is extracted; other timepoints (e.g. 24 hours, 1 month, 3 months) are handled in separate analyses of this review.
positive_direction: A positive effect size means the single sympathetic nerve block group had LOWER pain scores (less pain) at 14 days than the standard care group — i.e. the block reduced pain.
search_queries: sympathetic nerve block randomized controlled trial pain score
stellate ganglion block versus standard care pain outcome trial
lumbar sympathetic block single injection pain intensity VAS trial
inclusion_criteria: Human study in which patients received a single sympathetic nerve block (any target: stellate ganglion, lumbar sympathetic chain, celiac/splanchnic plexus, thoracic sympathetic, etc.) for any painful condition
Includes a comparison group receiving standard care, usual treatment, sham, or placebo injection
Reports any quantitative pain-intensity outcome at or near 14 days (approximately 1-3 weeks) that can be converted into an effect size
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, narrative review, editorial, opinion piece, case report, or purely theoretical/protocol paper)
No comparison between a sympathetic block (treatment) condition and a standard care / sham / control condition
No quantitative outcome data usable for an effect size (no means with SDs/SEs/CIs, t or F statistics, proportions, or odds ratios)
Completely unrelated to sympathetic nerve blockade or to pain outcomes
moderators_to_extract: Anatomical target of the sympathetic block (stellate ganglion, lumbar, celiac, other)
Underlying pain condition (CRPS, cancer pain, postherpetic neuralgia, ischemic/vascular pain, other)
Comparator type (active standard care vs sham/placebo injection)
Pain scale used (VAS vs NRS vs other)
effect_size_note: User explicitly requested pooling as a mean difference (MD) on the raw pain-score scale. Extract post-intervention means and SDs (or convert from SE/CI/IQR) at the ~14-day timepoint only; sign effects so that a positive MD indicates lower pain (benefit) in the sympathetic block arm. If a study reports multiple pain measures at 14 days, prefer the primary/overall pain-intensity scale.
